title: Service Spend Recognition on Extension Deposits for Vehicle Purchase Agreements
content:
## Recognition of service customers

A buyer's customer-pay service spend sets a service-spend share of the extension deposit taken on a reserved deal under the Vehicle Purchase Agreements. The spend is read from the buyer's service account ledger in **Service Accounts and Repair Orders**. It is the customer-pay labor lines and customer-pay parts lines charged on the account, at the amounts charged.

### The share

- Customer-pay labor and parts charged in the last 12 whole months before the handling date total **at least 1000.00** US dollars: the service-spend share is **90 percent**.
- They total **at least 500.00 but less than 1,000.00**: the share is **95 percent**.
- Otherwise no service-spend share applies.

A labor or parts line falls in the last 12 whole months when fewer than 12 whole calendar months have passed from its line date to the handling date. A month is whole once the same day of the month is reached. Lines on any other basis than customer pay are not included.

### Boundary cases (hypothetical totals)

| Customer-pay labor and parts in the window | Service-spend share |
|---|---|
| 1,250.00 | 90 percent |
| 1,000.00 | 90 percent |
| 999.99 | 95 percent |
| 500.00 | 95 percent |
| 499.99 | None |
| 0.00 (no customer-pay lines in the window) | None |

### Questions answered

- **Does a parts line count on its own, without labor?** Yes. Labor lines and parts lines charged on customer pay are added together.
- **Does work closed thirteen months before the handling date count?** No. Twelve whole months have already passed since its line date, so it is outside the window.
